Ada: Heads up — I found a weird NDCG drop in the rerank eval when bringing up the new quantized-v3. Small batches only (batch_size <= 4).

ci-bot: CI flaky: eval-runner / embeddings-rerank (ubuntu-22) failed: ndcg@10 decreased by 4.7% (threshold 2.0%). See job 4821.

Mike: repro steps? is this failing locally or only in CI?

Ada: Only reliably on CI image. Quick repro attached below.

Ada: ```python
# minimal repro (python3.10, transformer runtime stub)
from runner import RerankEvalRunner
model = load_quantized_model('quant-v3-q4_0')
queries = load_queries('mteb-small.json')
cands = load_candidates('mteb-cands.json')
runner = RerankEvalRunner(model, batch_size=2, kv_cache_prune=True)
metrics = runner.eval(queries, cands, metrics=['ndcg@10','mrr'])
print(metrics)  # NDCG drop shows up here
```

Sophia: Interesting — I remember a kv-cache-related merge bug from last year where prefix lengths were not normalized when merging micro-batches. Could produce nondeterministic ranking ties.

Luis: Also seeing this: the CI ubuntu-22 image has numpy 1.25 vs 1.24 in local env. argsort stability changed slightly, so tie-break ordering can flip when candidate scores equal-ish after quantization.

Mike: So two contributing factors: (1) small batch + kv-cache prune causes prefix shift, (2) sort stability differences amplify tie ordering -> ndcg skew.

DevEx: Proposed quick mitigation: add deterministic tie-breaker (score, id) in the runner and normalize prefix lengths before batching. Also add a unit test that asserts ndcg within eps for small-batch quantized runs. Would help CI reliability. :thumbsup:

Ada: I'll open a PR with the test and a patch that forces stable_sort on the candidate indices and normalizes prefix_kv sizes. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/921 (WIP).

Mike: For the test, can we create a synthetic case that reproduces rank ties? e.g., add gaussian noise -> quantize -> round ties, assert deterministic ordering.

Sophia: Yes — synthetic is fast and isolates root cause. Also add a CI job matrix entry: quantized-v3 + batch_size=2 on ubuntu-22 to catch regressions.

Luis: I can dig into the runner's batching code tonight. My plan: 1) ensure kv-cache prefix normalization step runs before chunking, 2) use stable argsort (np.lexsort with id) so sort is consistent across numpy versions.

Ada: Awesome. Assigning follow-ups: Ada -> test + PR, Luis -> patch batching logic, Mike -> add synthetic tie test harness, Sophia -> CI matrix change. I'll mark the issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/issues/487 (kv-cache/ndcg-flake).

DevEx: Nice! Once PR lands, let's backfill a short note in the rerank dashboard explaining the root cause and the new deterministic tie-break. Link to dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/ndcg/regressions?issue=487
